meta.meaning: Rubric assessments of single resources against the ten checks and seven weighted categories. A record is evidence of an assessment, never an approval: approval is a separate record in docs/reports/academic-review/teacher-verifications.json. method 'ai-assisted' means an AI system read the page against the cited official documents; it is not a teacher review. Totals and bands are computed from the categories by the scorecard and are never stored here. Records are append-only: a reassessment is a new record with a new id; the newest record for a resource wins.

fields.resource: resource slug (file name without .md) in src/content/resources/
fields.assessor: 'AI-assisted (<model id>)' for ai-assisted; an author profile id with isReviewer: true covering the resource's boards and subject for human
fields.humanEvidence: human only: where the teacher's own record is kept (signed form reference, email date)
fields.contentSha256: sha256 of the resource file as assessed (LF line endings); a later edit makes the record stale (REVERIFICATION_REQUIRED)
fields.syllabus: { board, code, series } the page was assessed against
fields.sources: [{ title, url, localRef? }]: at least one on the board's official domain; localRef is the file name in the owner's 'resource check' folder (see source-manifest.json)
fields.categories: { <category id>: { points, evidence, reasoning } } for the seven categories; worked-answers-exam-alignment may be { applicable: false, reasoning }
fields.findings: [{ id, check, severity: critical|major|minor|advisory, hardStop: <code>|null, location, description, evidence, status: open|fixed|wont-fix, resolution }]
fields.limitations: what this assessment did not or could not check
fields.reassessmentOf: optional: the id of the earlier record this one replaces after a correction (the earlier record is kept)

sources.title: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 syllabus for 2026, 2027 and 2028, version 2

syllabus-alignment.evidence: Syllabus p.13: 2.1 Core 1; 2.2 Core 1-6, no Supplement; 2.3 Core 1-2, Supplement 3-4. The page table lists 2.1.1, 2.2.1-2.2.6, 2.3.1-2.3.4 with exactly these tiers ('Extended only' on 2.3.3, 2.3.4). None missing, none invented. Definitions of proton number, mass number and isotopes match the syllabus wording. 'version 2 (August 2026)' matches p.58.
syllabus-alignment.reasoning: Coverage and tiering complete and correct; half a point off because the outcome column paraphrases the syllabus without saying so (F1).

factual-accuracy.evidence: Particle table +1/1, 0/1, -1/'1/1840 (negligible)' (true ratio about 1/1836, page says 'roughly'). Element/compound/mixture definitions and separation table correct. The 3.2 cross-reference to 1/12 of a carbon-12 atom matches p.14. Isotope chemistry explanation matches 2.3 Supplement 3.
factual-accuracy.reasoning: No factual errors found; half a point held for notation ambiguity (F3, F4).

worked-answers-exam-alignment.reasoning: Every worked answer correct and Extended-only items labelled; half a point held because the claim that a plain average 'scores no credit' was not checked against a mark scheme.

depth-teaching-value.evidence: Ten worked examples cover every outcome; misconception callouts (O2 is an element; 'pure' is not 'element'; ionic lattice is not a mixture); Ar sense check; common errors; FAQ; next steps to practice, bonding guides and 0620 Core/Extended diagnostics.
depth-teaching-value.reasoning: Strong for the declared scope; one point off because the page has no self-test items of its own.

source-traceability.evidence: The 'Official syllabus' section names the 0620 2026-2028 syllabus, version 2 (August 2026), sub-topics 2.1-2.3, without a URL in the body; the ledger records the correct 697205 PDF. Examples are generic; no reproduced past-paper text found.
source-traceability.reasoning: Accurate, specific citation; not linked in the body (F6).

clarity-accessibility.evidence: Logical headings; tables for outcomes, particles, classification; all 12 figures have specific alt text consistent with the text. 'Ar' used for both relative atomic mass and argon; signed-charge ion rule vs '16 + 2' in WE3; two isotope figures placed after WE10.
clarity-accessibility.reasoning: Clear and accessible; one point off for notation and figure placement (F3-F5).

editorial-completeness.evidence: author marlbridge-academic-team; reviewer nouman-ahmed (isReviewer, Chemistry, Cambridge); reviewStatus reviewed (D-379 credit); publishedDate 2026-10-04. reviewNote records no scope; no teacher-verifications.json record; description ends 'shells and isotopes, worked.'
editorial-completeness.reasoning: Fields complete and consistent; no documented verification and an awkward description (F7).

sources.title: Cambridge International AS & A Level Psychology 9990 syllabus for 2024, 2025 and 2026, version 1

syllabus-alignment.evidence: Every named item is in Option 1 content (pp.27-31): negative symptoms and Freeman et al. syllabus-alignment.reasoning: Accurate, complete alignment for what is tested; deducted for currency (F5): the series ends with November 2026 and the page says nothing about 2027 onwards.

factual-accuracy.evidence: Negative symptoms list, negative triad, tricyclic vs SSRI mechanisms, variable-ratio reinforcement, systematic desensitisation, applied tension for blood-injury-injection phobia, negative reinforcement of compulsions, Y-BOCS 10 items × 0-4 = 0-40, Lovell et al. random allocation all correct.
factual-accuracy.reasoning: No material error; small precision points (F3 uncertain, F4). Study details beyond syllabus titles checked from subject knowledge, scored conservatively.

worked-answers-exam-alignment.evidence: Paper 3 (p.51): three questions worth 14 marks and an essay of 6 + 10. Page Section A: Q1 2+4, Q2 3+2, Q3 3 = 14; Q4 6+10 = 16; total 30 = 'Each specialist option is out of 30 marks' (p.10). Essay on 1.4, a different topic from the short answers. Command words all in the p.54 table. Answers given for every question.
worked-answers-exam-alignment.reasoning: Tariffs and answers accurate; deducted for a top-band-only levels scheme on 4(b) (F1) and a Paper 4 section that does not mirror Paper 4 Section A (F2).

depth-teaching-value.evidence: 4(b) indicative content develops effectiveness, limits, idiographic vs nomothetic, reductionism, practicality, conclusion; 'Where marks are usually lost' gives five concrete errors; scenario and methods items.
depth-teaching-value.reasoning: Good exam-focused value; coverage is a sample of the option (F6).

source-traceability.evidence: 'Official syllabus' section links the 634461 PDF and names Specialist Option 1 and section 4. Studies cited by author and year as on p.26. Disclaimer: not taken from any past paper.
source-traceability.reasoning: Traceable; originality against the past-paper archive not verified.

clarity-accessibility.evidence: Clear H2 sections; bold question numbers with [n] tariffs; numbered answers; no images; internal links resolve to existing resources.
clarity-accessibility.reasoning: Well organised; mark points inline as '(1)' in dense paragraphs.

findings.description: The second part of Q4 (why isotopes have identical chemical properties) is 0620 Supplement (Extended) content, but it is unlabelled and the tier note says every other question is answerable by a Core candidate. Required for 5070, so 5070 students are not misled.
findings.evidence: Page line 48: 'All other questions are answerable by a 0620 Core candidate.' Q4: 'explain why isotopes of the same element have identical chemical properties. [3]'. 0620 p.13, 2.3 Supplement column: '3 State that isotopes of the same element have the same chemical properties because they have the same number of electrons'. Verified by the lead.
